chunks.text: You probably have seen this issue with retrieval augmented generation systems. Let's say you have a document with different versions. You create text chunks and store them in a vector store. But at query or retrieval time, you get chunks from all of these documents based on your query. That will confuse your LLM because it has no way of

differentiating between different documents. A simple solution is to add reliable metadata to each chunk. But the question is how do you get that metadata? There are multiple different approaches. But one of the simpler one is to extract metadata directly from the unstructured data that is present in your text documents. And

for that you can use something like lang extract which will convert unstructured data into structured data using the power of large language models. I personally like lang extract because you can define a custom schema which is extremely helpful if you want to control the quality of your metadata. I created a detailed video on this, but in this

video I'm going to show you how you can add metadata to your retrieval augmented generation system and improve its retrieval accuracy. So this is an opensource project from Google. It's not an official Google product, but it uses powerful LLMs like Gemini series for extraction of structured data from unstructured

documents. And it also has this very neat visualization tool. They just added support for other API providers including local models that you can run through Olama. Okay, so in this video we're going to build a retrieval augmented generation system that is going to be using lang extract to enhance both the metadata and hence

filtering the documents that are going to be used by the LLM to process the user query. In the rest of the video, we're going to look at a concrete example of how you can use lang extract to convert unstructured text files into structured metadata. and then how do you use this metadata to filter out results for your retrieval

augmented generation system. Okay, so we needed to import certain packages. Details are going to be in the video description. This code is going to be available to you through a GitHub link. But right now, we're going to load our API keys. Specifically, I'm going to be using Gemini 2.5 Flash. So you will need to get your Gemini API key for this to

work. Next, we need sample data. So in this case, I created the sample data. There are a couple of different examples. So this is the API reference documentation version 2.0. this is storage services guide. and troubleshooting guide for authentication errors. [snorts] Each of this unstructured file has ID, title, and then raw unstructured text.
